content:
Apple's home products — primarily the HomePod mini and Apple TV — have been the subject of much discussion over the past few years. The reason is simple: existing models are 4 to 6 years old.

Siri has reportedly been a bottleneck for new hardware launches — but now that Siri AI has finally arrived, we should soon see Apple start rolling out new home products. Here's what's already been reported.

Coming Soon

First up are the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. Based on current reporting, both of these products should debut later this fall.

The HomePod mini is expected to upgrade from the S5 chip to a new S9 chip, or potentially even better. There may be a few new colour options, a new wireless chip — likely the N1 that debuted on last year's iPhone — along with some audio improvements. The hardware upgrades will be modest, but what people are really hoping for is that the new HomePod mini will support Siri AI, making it a much more capable smart assistant.

As for the Apple TV 4K, it should upgrade from the A15 Bionic to the A17 Pro. To be honest, that feels somewhat dated, since the A17 Pro is itself a 3-year-old chip, but that's what the current reporting indicates. Hopefully the final product will feature a newer chip. Either way, this chip upgrade should bring it up to the spec required to support Siri AI, and should allow it to run some Apple Intelligence features on-device. There are also reports that the remote's design will see some adjustments.

Currently the HomePod mini retails for US$129, and the Apple TV 4K starts at US$199. Those are the prices Apple set after its price hike in June, so let's hope they stay the same when the new hardware arrives.

Later

Apple's first smart home hub device has been in development for some time. Reportedly there are two versions: one is just a screen that can be mounted on the wall via a magnetic system; the other has a speaker base attached — similar to the Google Nest Hub.

The product is expected to launch sometime between "October and early next year," so theoretically it could show up alongside the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. But to play it safe, I'm categorising it as later.

It will feature a 7-inch square display and run an entirely new operating system called homeOS (at least internally). The OS will allow the device to conduct FaceTime calls, interact with Siri AI, manage smart home devices, and more. This device, which many have dubbed the "HomePad," will be equipped with an A18 chip.

Also coming later is a possible update to the full-size HomePod. We don't have a release timeline for this product yet, but it will almost certainly feature an updated chip to support Siri AI to some extent. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has reported that this product is in development.

Further Out

Looking beyond late 2026/early 2027, Apple still has a few more home products in the pipeline.

The company is preparing to launch its first smart home accessories: a security camera and a smart home doorbell. Beyond offering smart home software, Apple is officially getting into making physical products. No firm release timing is known yet; you can read more about it here.

Finally, Apple will release a higher-end version of the aforementioned smart home display device. This version will feature a robotic arm and a larger 9-inch display, described as a desktop robot.

  • AirPods Pro 3 (twice the noise-cancelling performance of the AirPods Pro 2!)
  • Anker Nano 45W Smart Display Fast Charger
